messages:
maya (Support): fyi high-priority from ACME — multiple 503s + latency spikes on their Dedicated cluster dc-eu-02. tenant=acme-corp. window ~2024-03-15T09:12Z-09:22Z. example request ids: req-4f3a9c, req-4f3a9d, req-4f3aa1. they can reproduce with a simple curl but it sometimes succeeds.

jordan (SRE): thanks. can you paste the curl they used and a sample response (headers + body)? Also need target pod names / nodes and whether pods restarted.

acme-customer: here is minimal repro we run from their infra (we redacted token):

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "x-tenant: acme-corp" \
  -H "x-request-id: req-4f3a9c" \
  -X POST https://dc-eu-02.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"ping"}' --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 30

Response we sometimes see:
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
content-type: application/json
{x: "backend overloaded"}

maya (Support): they said affected pods match deployment inference-embedder-v2, pod names inference-embedder-v2-5f8gh, inference-embedder-v2-5f8gk. node reported as compute-12. no crashloop, but one pod had a restart at 09:15:02 UTC.

priya (eng-runtime): ok first-pass checklist for repro bundle: include kubectl describe pod, kubectl logs (both current and -p), kubelet journal on the node, dmesg, nvidia-smi samples for the window, and any edge-proxy/nginx logs for that host. Also include request ids in a plain file so we can correlate traces.

jordan (SRE): commands to collect logs (support will run from our bastion):

# pod logs
kubectl -n acme-corp logs deployment/inference-embedder-v2 --since=20m --tail=500 > /tmp/inference-embedder-logs.txt
# previous container logs if restarted
kubectl -n acme-corp logs inference-embedder-v2-5f8gh -p > /tmp/inference-embedder-prev.txt || true
# describe to capture events
kubectl -n acme-corp describe pod inference-embedder-v2-5f8gh > /tmp/pod-describe.txt

# on node compute-12 (ssh via support bastion)
ssh ubuntu@compute-12 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2024-03-15 09:00:00" --until "2024-03-15 09:30:00" -o cat' > /tmp/kubelet-journal.txt
ssh ubuntu@compute-12 'sudo dmesg --ctime | sed -n "1,200p"' > /tmp/dmesg.txt
ssh ubuntu@compute-12 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 2 -f /tmp/nvidia-smi-sample.csv &' 

maya (Support): can someone run the redwood diag collect for this tenant/time window? we have an internal tool redwood-diagnostic. sample usage below — it packages pod logs, node artifacts, and kv-caches. scrub tokens before upload.

priya (eng-runtime): example (run on our bastion):

redwood-diagnostic collect \
  --tenant acme-corp \
  --cluster dc-eu-02 \
  --since "2024-03-15T09:00:00Z" \
  --until "2024-03-15T09:30:00Z" \
  --pods inference-embedder-v2 --output /tmp/acme-dc-eu-02-20240315.tar.gz

Please make sure the bundle includes a file requests.txt with the request ids (req-4f3a9c, req-4f3a9d, req-4f3aa1).

sam (oncall): on it. I'll collect node-level metrics and vgpu traces. also check for OOMs and container OOM-score adjustments. starting collection now; will attach link when uploaded.

acme-customer: one extra data point — their app saw a token auth error immediately before 503s for req-4f3aa1. header we saw: 
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"
then later 503 for same request id on retry.

jordan (SRE): interesting — could be auth proxy temporarily rejecting then downstream overloaded. please include proxy/nginx logs on that node and the API gateway (pod redwood-gateway-eu-01).

maya (Support): can you also run a reproducible curl that includes full headers and timings so we can pass things to proxy/trace team?

curl -v -w "\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\nTIME_CONNECT:%{time_connect}\nTIME_STARTTRANSFER:%{time_starttransfer}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "x-tenant: acme-corp" -H "x-request-id: req-4f3aa1" -X POST https://dc-eu-02.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"ping"}' --max-time 30 > /tmp/curl-output.txt 2>&1

priya (eng-runtime): once bundle is uploaded, attach the S3 link here. we'll grep for the request ids and follow traces into runtime logs (kv-cache misses, batch sizes, kernel errors). also check if any GPU ECC errors in dmesg or nvidia-smi.

diag-bot: debug bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-debug/acme/dc-eu-02/2024-03-15/acme-dc-eu-02-20240315.tar.gz (permissions: private). link valid for 7 days.

sam (oncall): downloaded bundle and started correlation. initial findings: within window there are intermittent spikes in GPU compute utilization on compute-12 that coincide with large batch submissions from tenant acme-corp, followed by a short period where the gateway started returning 503s. collecting more traces now (kv cache hit/miss counts and batch sizes).

jordan (SRE): great. next steps: 1) confirm whether gateway saw a surge in concurrent inflight requests (attach gateway metrics), 2) check runtime batcher logs for sudden large batches, 3) confirm no node-level thermal throttling or ECC errors.

maya (Support): I'll keep ACME updated: we'll share a follow-up with timeline and whether we need reserved capacity bump or batching throttles. thanks all. :thumbsup:

acme-customer: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll standby for any more logs or a short screen share if needed.
